description: I’m a solo participant with a background in healthcare and applied data science. My project, Precipitation Trend Explorer, uses NASA GPM IMERG data to compare annual precipitation trends around Metro Manila and Metro Cebu, Philippines, from 2001 to 2024. The interactive notebook helps students explore how changing the study area or time period affects the estimated trend and its uncertainty.
summary: Precipitation Trend Explorer helps students test claims about long-term precipitation using NASA satellite data. The interactive notebook compares annual precipitation from 2001 to 2024 in two study areas in the Philippines, around Metro Manila and Metro Cebu. Users can choose a study area and date range to view annual totals, fitted trends, and confidence intervals. Moving the start year from 2001 to 2010 reversed the direction of both fitted trends. Across 15 exploratory start years, every confidence interval for the difference between the two trends included zero. The tool shows how the choice of dates can change an estimated trend and how confidence intervals help students interpret that change.
details:
I developed Precipitation Trend Explorer as an interactive Python notebook using pandas, SciPy, Matplotlib, and ipywidgets. It compares two geographic study areas in the Philippines, around Metro Manila and Metro Cebu, using 576 monthly NASA GPM IMERG Final Run V07 precipitation estimates exported through Giovanni. The notebook converts each monthly precipitation rate to a total using the number of hours in that month, sums the monthly totals by year, and fits a linear trend for each area. To compare the slopes directly, it fits a trend to the annual Manila-minus-Cebu differences.

Classroom exercise. Select both areas for 2001–2024 and ask whether the evidence supports the claim that annual precipitation increased faster around Cebu. Move the start year to 2010 while keeping the end year at 2024. Both fitted slopes switch from positive to negative, and the confidence interval for the difference includes zero in both periods. The 15-window overview highlights the selected start year so students can see whether the estimated direction holds across other date choices.

Scope and limitations. The study areas are geographic boxes around the two metro areas. The confidence intervals assume independent annual regression errors. The 15 windows share observations, and the intervals apply to each window individually. The overview is exploratory.

SI use. I used ChatGPT to help plan the project, interpret the analysis, draft and revise the notebook code, prepare the slides, and generate the cover and team artwork. The precipitation estimates come from the original NASA Giovanni exports.
